narrative.summary: The Marshall Islands has no AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. The main relevant instrument is the Personal Data Protection Act 2025, which applies data protection principles to core Government ministries and agencies and makes the Economic Policy, Planning and Statistics Office (EPSSO) the competent authority; it has no AI-specific provisions. The rest of the 2025 digital-law package (cybersecurity, cybercrimes, electronic transactions, digital identity and telecommunications reform) does not address AI. The Nitijela is the main source of relevant law, and no national AI body or strategy has been identified.
lead_institutions: Economic Policy, Planning and Statistics Office (EPSSO)
narrative.review_notes: The Nitijela's legislation portal, including the 2025 public laws, was searched and the Personal Data Protection Act 2025 was checked against its official text; the 2025 cybersecurity, cybercrime and digital laws contain no AI provisions. Not yet verified from the official text: material on the government portal and of the banking commission and the education system, and the certification date of the data protection law.

instruments.issuing_authority: Nitijela (Parliament) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
instruments.publisher_name: Nitijela (Parliament) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
instruments.current_status: Enacted as Public Law 2025-43 and codified as Title 6, Chapter 4 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code. The Nitijela's codified text gives a commencement date of October 7, 2025, while section 418 provides that the Act takes effect twelve months after the date of certification; the certification date is not printed in the text.
instruments.scope: Core Government ministries and agencies that collect, use, store, process, disclose or transfer personal data of natural persons in the Republic; excludes law enforcement, national intelligence and national security purposes.
instruments.summary: The Marshall Islands' first personal data protection law, applying only to core Government ministries and agencies. It sets six principles (legitimate purpose, data minimisation, accuracy, retention, integrity and security, accountability), names the Economic Policy, Planning and Statistics Office (EPSSO) as the competent authority with powers to issue guidance and regulations, and gives residents a right to sue a ministry or agency for injunctions or corrective orders but not damages. It also requires ministries to run complaint processes, report yearly to EPSSO, and allows data sharing between agencies under a safe harbour; it contains no provisions specific to AI or automated decision-making.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law governing how government bodies process personal data, including by automated means; relevant to any public-sector AI use.
metadata_gaps: Date of certification (section 418 sets effect twelve months after certification)

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The laws and bills, national government, ministries and regulators of the Marshall Islands were searched for AI laws, strategies, guidelines and guidance. Apart from the Personal Data Protection Act 2025, which covers government handling of personal data, no qualifying document was found; the 2025 cybersecurity, cybercrime and other digital laws contain no AI provisions.

Method note (original): This review was carried out on 13 October 2026, but Parliament's legislation portal blocks automated access and the banking commission's and health ministry's websites could not be accessed, so no official document could be read. leads.note: General cybersecurity framework law of the 2025 digital-law package (with the Digital Transformation and Identity Verification Act 2025 and the Electronic Transactions Act 2025). Official text on rmiparliament.org could not be reached on 2026-10-13 (captcha/403); only a PacLII bill copy was discoverable. Not AI-specific as far as known; check the official text for any AI provisions before recording. Update 2026-10-18: the official codified text (40 MIRC Ch. 4, Source: P.L. 2025-0027, Commencement: April 21, 2025) at https://rmiparliament.org/cms/images/LEGISLATION/PRINCIPAL/2025/2025-0027/2025-0027_1.pdf opened and was searched; it contains no artificial-intelligence provisions, so it stays a lead (out of scope as a general cybersecurity law). The Digital Transformation and Identity Verification Act 2025, Electronic Transactions Act 2025, Telecommunications (Reform) Act 2025 and Cybercrimes Act 2025 (P.L. 2025-40) official texts were also searched and contain no AI provisions.
